But RealDstIO.ts throws native Node.js errors (from fs.readFileSync, fs.statSync, etc.), NOT DstError instances. The DstError class IS imported at RealDstIO.ts line 6 but is never used anywhere in the file — it is dead code. MockDstIO correctly throws new DstError(..., code). This means error instanceof DstError checks would pass for MockDstIO but fail for RealDstIO, breaking the contract that code paths behave identically. | Alternative: Wrap native Node.js errors into DstError instances in every RealDstIO method that performs I/O. For example: readFile should catch Node.js ENOENT and throw new DstError(..., 'ENOENT'). Or add a private wrapper method: private wrapError(e: unknown): never { if (e && typeof e === 'object' && 'code' in e) throw new DstError((e as Error).message, (e as any).code); throw e; } and use it in every fs-calling method. | Risk: Test code and pipeline consumers that rely on error instanceof DstError for error-type discrimination will get silent false-negatives under RealDstIO, allowing logic bugs to escape into production. The dead DstError import (RealDstIO.ts line 6) confirms this breakage was unintentional.
